source: And his death was only one small part of my nightmare.
But... no matter the cost, being able to change his fate this much...
It's a victory, albeit a small one.
Even so, I won't live much longer now.
Unless I find a way to stop whoever's killing me, Father and I can never survive together and live on.
I'll just be returned to the beginning again... and Hamlet will still be a threat to Father's life.
I've got to find someone who believes me about this assassin so I can plan further.
Ophelia! There you are. There's something important we need to discuss with Father.
There is nothing left for me in Elsinore.
Even if I leave for Paris, I feel the knowledge that I would one day return would overshadow the trip.
I never desire to return to Elsinore again. And I know not why we linger here.
When you summoned us, Father, you were right. We should have left long ago.
This castle is a wretched place. A sorrowful place.
Well, it seems there's a drop of wisdom left in my bones yet.
Ophelia, my love, what do you say? Your brother and I desire to leave. What of you?
Shall we make preparations?
Flee Elsinore with my family?

source: My son, I know that you are distressed, but this is a drastic response.
Life at court can be difficult, it's true. Many of the nobility aren't able to handle such pressure.
But I have respect and influence here at Elsinore. People desire my counsel.
Do you? Do you truly?
I have no reason to believe otherwise. The court still values my advice.
No. I am needed here. I cannot in good conscience leave.
If you have some proof to the contrary, I'll gladly hear it. But I find the notion unlikely.
Ophelia. We have matters we must discuss as a family.
Yes. When I called our first meeting, I was hoping your heart would change, Father.
I'm merely sorry it happened in such a strange and cruel way.
As am I. But at least it has made the decision a simple one.
Ophelia? What do you say?
I've been struggling with similar thoughts, I must admit.
Ophelia, what are your thoughts?
I cannot leave, Father.
What? But for weeks, you've been pleading to leave for Paris!
Yes. But that was meant to be temporary. The remains of the summer, at best.
I always knew, or believed, that I would return here.
There's... someone very important to me I couldn't bear to leave.
Not just yet. Not until I know if the way I feel for her can ever be returned.
A lover? Come now, Laertes. How frivolous of you.
Apologies, Father. But my mind is made up. I love her.
(Does he mean—Brit?)
Very well. We'll stay for now. But the moment your 'heart' has made up its mind, we'll depart.
Brit is dead.
I'm not certain what the two of you knew—but I loved her.
And I've loved her ever since she came to Elsinore. I had hoped to leave her safely behind as I went to Paris.
And maybe, when I'd returned, I'd come for her, even if her father wouldn't approve, even if she was promised elsewhere...
Now, suddenly, that dream is gone.
I'm so sorry. I am.
Lady Brit has been uncovered as a traitor to the court, thanks to Ophelia.
But this has dealt me a devastating blow.
She wanted to kill Ophelia.
I am truly sorry, Laertes, that it turned out this way.
I have had a moment in which to reflect upon all that's occurred lately, and it has removed some of the doubt from my heart.
Something happened between His Highness and I, and it gave me a much-needed chance to reflect on the way Claudius feels about me.
I now have cause to fear my very life may be in jeopardy if we linger here.
That performance I saw—it was—unlike anything I'd ever witnessed.
To have your worst fears about yourself echoed back at you as truth... it was a mockery. Insult in the highest form.
Much as it pains me to believe this, my use to this dynasty has come to a close, I think.
Now, of course, I regret that I invested everything we had into King Hamlet's war.
We still own a little land and a single estate. It is old, but sufficient, and the three of us will be together there.
Perhaps we can make some new life for ourselves, though much of our current comfort will be lost.
I think you're both correct. Let's leave together. We'll be happier on our own. I know it.
(Even if this world only lasts a short while.)
Then we shall depart as soon as possible.
Necessary preparations ought to be made—but of course, there is little use in me making them, as I owe the court nothing further.
Let us gather our belongings, Father. I'll have Reynaldo staff a carriage.
I cannot. I need to remain here in Elsinore for the time being.
For what possible purpose?
I'm sorry—I cannot say.
Then we shall depart without you.
When the time is right, you may join us. We'll send for you as often as we can, certainly.
This is only a temporary parting, Ophelia. We shall meet one another soon. I know it.
They all think me a fool.
I am a fool. They despise me.
I've given everything I could. Everything!
And this is what it's worth?
...Nothing at all.
Is any of this real?
Does any of it matter? Or is this all but a dream?
It must be a dream... Yes, all a dream...
It's no good. I haven't woken up.
Then if they hate me so—if this is to be my life—
I want none of it. I care not a whit.
King Hamlet, if what you wrote in your notes is true...
There's a way to be reborn again, to try once more to right these wrongs...
My love, all the necessary preparations have been made.
The carriage is loaded outside the walls. Are you prepared?
As well as I can be, Father.
Something has become alarmingly clear in these last few hours.
Elsinore is no longer our home.
And so we shall go on and forge a new home, the three of us.
We may lack the deep coffers and guards and gardens, but... I have the two of you. And that's all I've ever needed.
That's wealth enough for me, I think.
Yes. The three of us together.
And to think, how suddenly things can change!
There... are things we leave behind, certainly.
But it's time to replace those things with a world of our own creation.
Let's go. Father. Ophelia.
I'm ready.
I didn't make it twenty acres in the carriage before I was pulled back in time.

source: (Though... as things stand now, I shall never see what comes of this world.)
Father is still alive, locked away in a cell... accused of being a spy.
That means Hamlet can't get to him, but...
This... doesn't feel like a victory.
I brought this fate upon him... I have to be able to bring an even better one.
I need to visit him.
Oh. Ophelia. Hello.
It's good to see you, Father. Even if it's like this.
You know, Ophelia, I've been thinking.
The sorts of idle things an old man dreams about when he begins to contemplate the end of his life.
Namely, about your mother. Were she still here... what she'd think of me. Of the way I've lived my life.
I've served the throne faithfully for so many years. So many times I wondered what all that unflagging allegiance was worth.
Would she have wanted me to lie to the king? Would she have wanted me to... betray a promise?
Some time in the future, I had been thinking I ought to take you to summer somewhere outside of Elsinore.
I expect the King will exile us soon. I won't stay in this cell forever. And then... we'll have our chance.
We'll leave Elsinore and we'll never return.
Look at me. Don't cry, love.
And I'm not going anywhere.
I won't be executed. Not over this. This is merely Claudius's pettier side at work. Rest assured of that.
Unfortunately, for now, I must ask you leave me be. I don't want you caught up in all this. The King mustn't see you speaking with me.
I'm sorry. I'll leave you be, father.
I want you to take this and keep it safe.
It's a key. It opens the chest in my room. I keep—kept—it on me at all times.
This chest cannot be opened via any other method. It contained those notes, but they're long gone now.
Please take it. If Bernardo finds it, then they'll surely search my room, yours, and Laertes'. And I don't want to give them cause to do that.
Keep it close to you.
(So Father has a key on him. Perhaps, in the future, there's a way to examine that chest before it comes to this...)
At least for now... my father is alive. That's what matters.
Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
Blessed art thou among women...
And blessed is the fruit of thy womb...
I say, I didn't know you were a Catholic, Bernardo! Aren't those rather detested around these parts?
... Do you mind?
I wish to be alone.
Oh, please, don't mind me. Carry on, carry on. Terribly sorry. I'll be like a mouse's shadow over here. Promise.
... Holy Mary, Mother of God...
Pray for us sinners now and at the hour of our death.
Well, then. What awful thing have you done this week that needs the Virgin's forgiveness?
Gone whoring? Been reading salacious literature? Caught embedded in a sheep?
...You're absolutely vile.
I have committed no sins that I know of.
And yet you come to pray outside of mass. Why is that?
My father was of the clergy. I, like him, am a man of God in spirit.
Seems a waste of time to me. Isn't the whole notion of the Christian God that he knows how you feel regardless?
We could be playing cards right now instead.
Did you come here merely to engage me in your frivolous opinions?
And besides, card games are a sin! I ought to refuse your temptations... and Irma's too, for that matter. It leads to drinking and dancing. Awful business.
(She always uses the trick deck anyhow...)
Hmm. No cards? No drinking, no dancing? Well then. What does your God promise you that's so very compelling in return?
Infinite bliss in the afterlife.
What, when you're dead? Rotten deal, if you ask me.
Mortal life is but a blink of an eye. As a soldier, I could die any day. But Heaven is eternal, and I will sit at God's side.
Hmm. Now that sounds like a slightly better wager.
Do you not speak to the Lord? Are you truly so uninvested in His word?
Oh, I don't much care what your Christ has to say, though he seems kind-intended enough. Where I come from, we have hundreds of gods.
